title: PTCG RL campaign foundations

sections.title: What the agent must do
sections.summary: The submitted program returns one fixed 60-card deck, then repeatedly chooses indices from the engine's current legal option list. The final objective is game outcome, not prize margin.
sections.why_it_matters: The policy should rank the legal options it actually receives instead of learning a huge fixed action vocabulary.

sections.title: Why memory is required
sections.summary: Opponent hands, prizes and deck order are hidden. Public logs and previous reveals may disappear from the current snapshot, so separate recurrent memory is kept for each player and episode.
sections.why_it_matters: A stateless policy can forget revealed cards, prior actions and public context that change the best move.

sections.title: What G1R proved
sections.summary: The environment now checks terminal state first, preserves every legal option and log event, validates compound actions, isolates recurrent state and retains auditable evidence.
sections.why_it_matters: Training on a wrong action or lifecycle contract would create convincing but unusable learning curves.

sections.title: What G2 must build
sections.summary: G2 converts public cards, players, events and legal options into model-ready tensors, then adds a compact entity-attention encoder, GRU memory, semantic option scorer, STOP-aware multi-select decoder and value head.
sections.why_it_matters: G2 is the bridge between a correct simulator adapter and any valid PPO trajectory.

sections.title: Why replay data is separated
sections.summary: Public replays are used for deck/meta intelligence, context coverage and diagnosis. Their actions are not PPO samples or behavior-cloning labels in v0.
sections.why_it_matters: This prevents selected public behavior from silently changing the approved reward-only learning boundary.

sections.title: Why strict gates are used
sections.summary: Reliability and important-matchup floors are checked before aggregate strength. A newer checkpoint is not automatically better, and unresolved evidence cannot replace the trusted anchor.
sections.why_it_matters: Self-play and small match samples can produce false improvements, cycles and catastrophic matchup regressions.

sections.title: Where work runs
sections.summary: Local work handles correctness and small tests. Private Kaggle notebooks handle heavy validation and bounded training smoke. Modal is reserved for approved main training.
sections.why_it_matters: The compute plan preserves budget while keeping every heavy result tied to committed code and durable artifacts.

boundaries: No episode JSON transfer before the immutable R1 plan is reviewed.
No PPO training before G2 and evaluation implementation review.
No Modal execution, deck freeze, submission or Git push without explicit approval.
